exposure: Maternal mitochondrial disease (m.3243A>G in the MTTL1 gene or m.12258C>A in the MT-TS2 gene)
cohort: 26 women with genetically confirmed mitochondrial disease and their 88 pregnancies
finding: Women with mitochondrial disease, particularly the m.3243A>G mutation, experience higher rates of obstetric complications, including miscarriage, GDM, and preterm delivery, with increased maternal heteroplasmy levels correlating with a higher risk of assisted operative vaginal delivery and CS.
mod_finding: For every unit increase in maternal heteroplasmy levels, there was a 26% increased risk of undergoing an assisted operative vaginal delivery and an 18% increased risk of undergoing a CS compared to a spontaneous vaginal delivery.
